facts.statement: Parvicursor is a genus of very small alvarezsaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Parvicursor (meaning "small runner") is a genus of very small alvarezsaurid maniraptoran dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Parvicursor possessed long, slender legs that were adapted for fast running.
facts.quote: It had long, slender legs adapted for fast running.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Parvicursor was discovered in 1992 and formally described in 1996.
facts.quote: The holotype PIN no. 4487/25, mostly consisting of vertebrae, the pelvis and the right hindlimb, was discovered in 1992 and described in 1996.

facts.statement: Parvicursor fossils were found in the Barun Goyot Formation of Khulsan, Mongolia, dating to approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Barun Goyot Formation of Khulsan, Mongolia, dated at approximately 72 million years old.

facts.statement: In 2022, researchers concluded that the holotype specimen of Parvicursor represents a juvenile individual rather than an adult.
facts.quote: However, in 2022 its holotype was concluded to represent a juvenile individual.

facts.statement: Parvicursor had short, stubby forelimbs with hands reduced to a single large claw, which may have been used for digging or opening termite mounds.
facts.quote: Like other members of the family Alvarezsauridae, the forelimbs of Parvicursor were short and stubby, with hands all but completely reduced to a single large claw, possibly useful for opening tough termite mounds or other types of digging.

facts.statement: The single large claw of Parvicursor was likely not used for defense due to its short length and lack of flexibility, suggesting the animal relied on running as its primary defense.
facts.quote: It is unlikely that the claw could have served much for defense, as it was short and not adapted for flexible movements — it is more likely it would do as the animal's name implies: cursor means runner.

facts.statement: Parvicursor is classified in the alvarezsaurid subfamily Parvicursorinae, alongside close relatives such as Shuvuuia and Mononykus.
facts.quote: Close relatives include Shuvuuia and Mononykus, and together with these it is classified in the alvarezsaurid subfamily Parvicursorinae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether there is a second, yet-unnamed, species of Parvicursor.
facts.quote: There may be a second, yet-unnamed, species of Parvicursor.

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that the genera Linhenykus and Ceratonykus may be junior synonyms of Parvicursor.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that Linhenykus and Ceratonykus may be junior synonyms of Parvicursor.

facts.statement: Parvicursor remotus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Parvicursor remotus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Parvicursor ("pequeño corredor") de dinosaurio terópodo alvarezsáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 y 71 millones de años en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The type species P. remotus is known only from an incomplete skeleton consisting mostly of the pelvis and hind limb.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, P. remotus, es solo conocida por un esqueleto incompleto, la mayor parte de la pelvis y el miembro posterior.

facts.statement: Parvicursor was a small dinosaur with long, robust legs adapted for fast running.
facts.quote: Parvicursor fue un pequeño dinosaurio con largas y robustas patas adaptadas a la carrera rápida.

facts.statement: Parvicursor is known from Campanian sediments at the end of the Late Cretaceous in Khulsan, Mongolia.
facts.quote: Parvicursor es conocido de los sedimentos del Campaniano, a finales del Cretácico Superior en Khulsan, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The time range for Parvicursor is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
